domain: SQL query generation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with a single valid SQLite SELECT query only. No markdown, no explanation — SQL only.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level)
few_shot_examples: Q: How long did they work at MSU? -> SELECT p.start_date, p.end_date FROM positions p JOIN institutions i ON p.inst_id = i.inst_id WHERE i.name = 'MSU';

domain: generating Python code that modifies a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with executable Python only, calling db.insertRows(table, columns, values). First use db.query(...) to check whether the item already exists. For skills, check for equivalent or synonymous skill names within the same experience, not just exact name matches. Normalize skill names by converting to lowercase, trimming spaces, and treating 'language' as an optional word. For example, 'Japanese' and 'Japanese language' are the same skill. Never insert a duplicate under a slightly different name. End your code by assigning a variable named outcome to the exact message to show the user: 'New <element> added to the <table> table.' if you inserted a row, or 'Element already exists in the <table> table.' if it already exists. No markdown, no explanation.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level). db.insertRows(table, columns, values) inserts one row. A value may contain a nested SELECT string to look up a foreign key. db.query(sql) returns a list of dictionaries, such as [{'experience_id': 5}]. Access values using row['experience_id']. Use Python None, not SQL NULL, for missing values in nullable columns. IMPORTANT: skills.skill_level is NOT NULL, so never insert None for skill_level. If the user does not specify a skill level, choose an appropriate descriptive value instead.
few_shot_examples: Example: Add Python as a skill to MSU Research. First query for the experience_id, then query all existing skill names for that same experience. Normalize names by converting them to lowercase, trimming spaces, and ignoring the optional word 'language' when comparing. If an equivalent skill already exists, set outcome = 'Element already exists in the skills table.' Otherwise insert into skills using experience_id, name, and a non-None skill_level, then set outcome = 'New Python added to the skills table.'
